findings.found: 2. BROKERAGE SERVICES AREA. This Contract applies to the purchase of any real property by Buyer located anywhere in the State of Colorado, including without limitation Larimer, Weld, and Boulder Counties.
findings.default_analysis: The services-area blank is filled region-wide, obligating the buyer to this broker for ANY purchase anywhere in the territory during the term. The blank could have named one county, one town, or one listing. Region-wide scope plus a backstop clause is how a buyer ends up owing a fee on a property the broker never touched.

findings.found: 7. COMPENSATION TO BROKER. Buyer agrees that Broker's Success Fee shall be 3% of the Purchase Price of any property acquired by Buyer during the term of this Contract, earned as set forth below.
findings.default_analysis: The compensation blank arrives pre-filled with a percentage. Buyer-broker compensation is negotiable and is not set by law or by any MLS rule; the blank could equally hold a flat fee, an hourly rate, or a lower percentage with a cap. Ask what the number would be if you proposed it.

findings.found: 7.3 ADDITIONAL COMPENSATION. If the Seller or the listing brokerage does not pay all or any portion of the Success Fee, Buyer shall pay Broker the unpaid balance at Closing.
findings.default_analysis: If the seller or listing brokerage does not pay, the buyer pays the entire unpaid fee at closing — on top of down payment and closing costs. The blank could have capped buyer liability, made the fee contingent on seller-side payment, or struck the backstop entirely. Exposure shown is the pre-filled percentage applied to the configured target price.

findings.found: 8. FEE EARNED ON DEFAULT. If Buyer defaults under any contract to purchase a property in the Services Area, the Success Fee is earned, due, and payable on the date of default, and the obligations of this Section survive the expiration or termination of this Contract.
findings.default_analysis: If the buyer defaults on a purchase contract, the broker's fee is still earned, due, and payable — the buyer pays for a closing that never happened, on top of any earnest money already lost. The blank could have limited the fee to transactions that actually close.
